newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebel attack shuts down oil pipeline in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Rebel attack shuts down oil pipeline in Colombia.

text.p: Leftist rebels dynamited an oil pipeline in northeastern Colombia on Sunday in a nationwide offensive against the government of President Ernesto Samper.

A statement from the 2nd Army Division in Norte de Santander province said all pumping operations along the 220,000-barrel per day Cano Limon-Covenas pipeline had been suspended in the aftermath of the attack by National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrillas.
The pipeline carries oil from the Cano Limon oil field operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp Plc to the Caribbean port of Covenas. It has been attacked more than 400 times since it opened in 1987.

In other developments, military spokesmen said 13 guerrillas were killed on Sunday in fighting across Colombia, including eight ELN fighters gunned down in a foiled attack on the small town of Guarne in northwestern Antioquia province.
At least one solider was killed in the fighting, which included skirmishes in central Boyaca province, the spokesmen said.
The ELN, Colombia's second-largest guerrilla group, was founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1996 and specialises in kidnappings and economic sabotage.

It declared a nationwide offensive or "armed strike" last Friday aimed at stepping up pressure for Samper to resign because of charges that his 1994 election campaign was financed with narcotics money.
The rebel communique announcing the offensive described Samper as a puppet of Colombian drug lords who is now seeking to curry favour with the United States by handing over power to the military.
The ELN offensive has featured sabotage attacks across much of the country since Friday and guerrilla roadblocks have paralysed transportation along many key highways throughout the country.
